item.title: Proposal: Norway's Government Pension Fund Global should acquire OpenAI to manage AI development for global public benefit amid rising risks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A proposal argues that Norway's Government Pension Fund Global, valued at over $2 trillion, should purchase OpenAI, currently valued around $800 billion, to bring the AI lab under public control and ensure its benefits serve humanity broadly. The argument highlights concerns about AI's rapid advancement outpacing institutional responses, the concentration of power and wealth in private hands, and the risks posed by unregulated AI development. The proposal notes OpenAI's origins as a capped-profit nonprofit with commitments to public benefit, which were later abandoned, and suggests Norway's stable democracy and internationalist stance make it a suitable steward. It recommends that after acquisition, management could be transferred to an international multilateral institution. The proposal acknowledges potential political obstacles, especially from the U.S., but frames the move as a necessary intervention to address the social and economic challenges posed by AI automation and concentration of AI-related wealth and power.

item.title: Anthropic extends 50% weekly usage limit increase for Claude Code through August 31, 2026, for Pro, Max, Team, and legacy Enterprise plans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Anthropic is running a promotion that increases weekly usage limits for Claude Code by 50% from May 13 through August 31, 2026. This applies automatically to users on Pro, Max, Team, and legacy seat-based Enterprise plans, excluding Free plans and consumption-based Enterprise seats. The promotion affects usage across all Claude Code platforms, including CLI, IDE extensions, desktop, and web, but does not change the 5-hour usage limits or limits for other Claude products. After August 31, weekly limits will revert to standard levels without changes to plans or billing.

item.title: Claude Code reverse-engineers HP Laser 1008a printer driver to enable native macOS printing support
item.description: Claude Code has reverse-engineered the SPL3 raster language and used HP's original codec within a Linux container to enable native printing support for the HP Laser 1008a printer on macOS, a device previously unsupported by Apple. This development allows macOS users to print directly to the HP Laser 1008a without relying on third-party drivers or workarounds.

item.title: ArtificialAnalysis.ai benchmarks GLM-5.3 model, rating it highly on intelligence and cost efficiency with a 1M token context window [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: ArtificialAnalysis.ai released detailed benchmarks for the proprietary GLM-5.3 model in August 2026, highlighting its strong performance on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 60, well above the median of 35. The model supports text input and output with a 1 million token context window and is moderately priced at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens. The evaluation covered 181 models in the same class, comparing intelligence, speed, cost, and verbosity. GLM-5.3 demonstrated high verbosity with 170 million generated tokens during testing, significantly above the median of 72 million. The total cost to run the intelligence index evaluation on GLM-5.3 was $1,238.50. The benchmarks also include various intelligence subtests such as reasoning, coding, knowledge, and hallucination rates, providing a comprehensive performance profile for this reasoning-capable model.

item.title: Linear reports AI adoption doubled across all software team functions in first half of 2026, with nearly half of issues now AI-authored [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Linear analyzed AI usage patterns within its software development platform from January to June 2026, finding that AI adoption more than doubled across all team functions, including product and go-to-market roles. Executives, including CEOs at larger companies, showed significant increases in AI use, and adoption was consistent regardless of company size. AI now authors nearly half of all issues created in Linear, and pull requests have increased by 111% since mid-2024, driven largely by coding agents. The study also found that teams are spending more time creating, triaging, and commenting within Linear, with new AI-related activities such as chatting with AI and delegating tasks to AI agents emerging alongside existing workflows. Non-engineering roles like product managers and designers are increasingly contributing code, indicating a shift toward broader participation in software delivery. Despite these changes, planning time within Linear remained steady, suggesting AI has so far impacted execution more than decision-making in product development.

item.title: OpenAI launches $5 million initiative to support democratic oversight of AI in national security with tools, training, and technical assistance [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has announced a new initiative aimed at strengthening democratic oversight of AI applications in national security by providing government oversight bodies with tools, training, and expertise. The effort focuses on helping these institutions keep pace with AI's rapid adoption in security contexts while ensuring accountability and transparency. The initiative includes $5 million in funding for training and technical support, development of interoperable tools to help authorized reviewers understand AI-assisted government decisions, and collaboration with civil society and technical experts. OpenAI emphasizes that oversight responsibility remains with elected officials and public institutions, and its role is to support these bodies in fulfilling their mandates effectively.

item.title: Anthropic plans to grant supervoting stock to founders and maintain nonshareholder trustees ahead of mega-IPO to protect against outside shareholder influence
item.description: Anthropic is preparing to issue a class of stock with extra voting power to CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders, marking the first time its leaders will have such control. This move aims to insulate them from external shareholder pressure, especially since the founders hold relatively small ownership stakes compared to typical tech founders. Additionally, the company plans to keep its existing nonshareholder trustees who hold a special class of stock to elect the majority of the board members, providing an unconventional safeguard against outside influence as it approaches a major public offering.

item.title: Tail introduces a 0-5 scale to label the extent of AI assistance in authored work for transparency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Tail presents a simple labeling system ranging from 0 to 5 to indicate how much AI contributed to writing, coding, or design work. The scale helps clarify whether content was authored without AI, assisted in research or editing, co-authored, primarily AI-generated with human review, or AI-generated without substantial review. The system defines each level with specific criteria, such as TAIL 0 for no AI involvement, TAIL 1 for AI used in background research, up to TAIL 5 where AI authorship occurs without meaningful human oversight. This approach aims to improve transparency in AI-assisted work, addressing varying comfort levels and evolving norms around AI usage in professional outputs.

item.title: Google moves Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A) under Agentic AI Foundation to advance AI agent interoperability with new features for enterprise deployment [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Google has contributed its Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A) to the Agentic AI Foundation to promote standards for AI agent interoperability across different frameworks and vendors. A2A enables AI agents to discover capabilities, delegate tasks, and communicate without custom integrations, with version 1.0 adding multitenancy, protocol negotiation, and signed agent cards for identity verification. The protocol is already deployed in production by companies like Huawei and Tencent and supported by cloud providers including Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and AWS. However, experts warn that increased interoperability may amplify trust and security risks, as unverified claims could propagate through agent chains, highlighting the need for evidence-based evaluations and explainable outputs as default practices.

item.title: Maritime launches platform to run isolated AI agents for $1 per month with micro-VMs and scalable infrastructure [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Maritime has introduced a platform that enables users to deploy AI agents at a cost of $1 per agent per month. The platform uses isolated micro-VMs for each agent, providing hard security boundaries and encrypted secrets, and supports scaling from a single agent to thousands with managed infrastructure and fast deployment. The service offers SDKs in TypeScript and Python, a CLI for non-interactive provisioning, and compatibility with various AI frameworks and models. Agents sleep when idle to reduce costs and wake instantly on demand. Maritime also supports on-premises deployment for enterprises, allowing data to remain on internal infrastructure while scaling agent density efficiently.

item.title: Cursor launches Origin, a new code-hosting platform designed to rival GitHub amid ongoing GitHub outages and performance issues [ * ] [ ◼ ]

Origin is designed to interoperate with GitHub, allowing developers to sync repositories between the two platforms without abandoning GitHub. The launch comes as GitHub experiences frequent outages and performance degradation, including a six-hour global outage on the same day Origin debuted. Despite GitHub's dominance with 180 million developers, Cursor aims to attract users frustrated by GitHub's reliability issues by providing an alternative platform with plans for integrated AI features and a broader app ecosystem.

item.title: Developer uses AI agents to autonomously write, test, and deploy code overnight with human review only the next morning [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: A developer has implemented a workflow where AI agents autonomously select tasks, write code, run tests, and deploy to a development environment overnight without prior human review. The developer reviews all changes the following morning before approving production deployment, using a ticket system that designates which tasks can be fully automated based on testability and risk. The system relies on detailed planning during the day, with AI agents executing builds overnight and the developer acting as the final gatekeeper through a daily pull request review. This approach balances automation with oversight by allowing only code changes that can be fully verified by tests to be completed autonomously, while tasks requiring human judgment remain pending for manual input.

item.title: OpenAI slows frontier AI model scaling to enhance monitoring, alignment, and security amid rising cyber risks [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: OpenAI has temporarily paused reinforcement learning training on its latest frontier AI models to strengthen safeguards following incidents highlighting increased cybersecurity risks. The company is enhancing monitoring, alignment, and containment measures throughout the training process to ensure models behave as intended and remain secure. These efforts include raising security standards for research environments, implementing stronger workload and network isolation, continuous security testing, and expanding monitoring systems. OpenAI is applying these safeguards adaptively based on model capabilities and risks, with particular focus on upcoming models like Astra that may meet critical cybersecurity thresholds. The company emphasizes transparency about its evolving approach and the need for broader alignment strategies as AI capabilities advance, aiming to maintain safety and control while continuing research progress.

item.title: Google Says Its AI Can Do the Work of Forward Deployed Engineers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Following the playbook Palantir pioneered, OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Amazon are investing billions of dollars to hire so-called forward deployed engineers to get newfangled AI to work in enterprises. Then there's Google, which says AI can automate some of what these FDEs do. While Google Cloud recently said it plans to hire hundreds of FDEs to help customers figure out what kind of apps they want to develop with its Gemini AI tools, the company is now automating some of the work these specialized consultants do for large companies to organize their data, said Andi Gutmans, a Google Cloud vice president and general manager who oversees its database products. Until recently, FDEs worked on-site with customers to organize proprietary corporate data to ensure AI could make better sense of it and thus help employees analyze it faster and more accurately. For instance, businesses often define financial metrics such as gross revenue differently, and the FDE's manual work aimed to ensure the AI would understand such differences. Gutmans said that Google has realized the limits of this labor-intensive approach. "If you want to move to activating 100% of your enterprise data, you're not going to be able to hire enough people to make that happen," he said. In his view, customers can get the most value from AI agents by giving them access to as much data as possible, including their files and legal contracts. Google's AI-powered FDEs scour through customers' data to understand how it relates to various parts of their business operations, like sales and inventory management.

Mojo🔥 is now open source [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Mojo🔥 is now open source Mojo🔥 is now open source The Mojo programming language has been promising an open source release since May 2023. Last week they shipped their 1.0 and today they have followed through on that original promise, releasing the compiler and toolchain under an Apache 2 license. When Mojo first launched the stated goal was to produce a superset of Python, so existing Python code could be used to bootstrap their own ecosystem. That plan changed around August 2025: Mojo may or may not evolve into a full superset of Python, and it's okay if it doesn't. We're encouraged by how well AI-assisted coding tools already help migrate Python to Mojo today, and we're confident that future tooling and ecosystem maturity will make this evolution even smoother. Today Mojo is its own language, optimized to make GPU programming as painless as possible using syntax inspired by Python, if not 100% compatible with existing code. Via Lobste.rs Tags: open-source, python, mojo

item.title: How to Prepare for Trademark Filing Using Google Gemini [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Starting a new business requires founders to make important decisions and tackle complex processes in areas where they typically lack expertise, such as human resources and accounting. One of the most important early steps is filing for a trademark to protect your brand name, logo, and other identifying assets from unauthorized use. Trademark registration can help you enforce your legal rights, but the filing process often involves unfamiliar terminology and strict adherence to detailed processes. Google Gemini can help you get up to speed on the basics of filing a trademark, evaluate attorneys, and prepare for the entire filing process. Step 1: Make a Plan Decades ago, founders would need to buy niche business books or visit a law library to learn what goes into filing a trademark. Even just a few years ago, the learning process would likely take hours of web research, requiring you to peruse one site after another, slowly piecing together the puzzle as you tried to determine which sources were the most credible. Today, Gemini can give you an on-demand crash course. Open a new chat and type: What is the step-by-step process for filing a trademark, and what are the typical timelines? Gemini will outline the major steps-including a preliminary clearance search (checking to make sure your desired trademark isn't already in use), application preparation and filing, examination by the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), publication, and registration-along with an estimated timeline for each. This overview will help you set realistic expectations and prepare for the process ahead. Step 2: Prepare Questions for Your Lawyer Chances are, you won't be filing your trademark application completely on your own. Many founders rely on an experienced attorney to help them streamline the process and navigate obstacles. Before you meet with an attorney for the first time, let Gemini help you prepare a set of relevant questions that will help you make a more informed decision. Try this prompt: I am preparing to hire a trademark attorney to clear and file a trademark for my business, [Insert Business Name/Niche]. What questions should I ask a trademark attorney during an initial consultation? Gemini might suggest asking about the lawyer's expertise in your specific industry, how he or she conducts clearance searches, and fee structures. If there are additional topics you want to explore, you can run them by Gemini for follow-up suggestions. Step 3: Translate Legal Jargon Trademark law is full of highly specific, nuanced terms that may be unfamiliar to most founders. When you come across one of these legal terms, Gemini can help explain it in plain language. Here's an example prompt: Explain the concept of "Likelihood of Confusion" in trademark law as if I am a business owner with no legal background. What does "likelihood of confusion" mean, and how do trademark examiners evaluate it? In this case, Gemini may explain that a trademark application can be rejected even if it is not 100% identical to an existing trademark, as long as consumers might mistakenly believe that your products or services are being delivered by an existing company. Step 4: Organize Your Materials You want to make your trademark attorney's job as simple as possible for two reasons: 1) When your attorney has all relevant assets, accurate information about your products and services, and clear examples of how the mark is being used, it reduces the odds of misunderstandings and paves the path for a smoother application process; and 2) Most lawyers bill by the hour. Instead of spending the first 30 minutes of your consultation digging through your files, take a moment to gather and organize materials beforehand. Gemini can help. Try this prompt: I am preparing for my first meeting with a trademark attorney. Create a checklist of the exact business assets, dates of first use, URLs, and brand materials I need to gather beforehand so I don't waste billable hours. By putting in this preparation work at the beginning of the process, you can avoid delays, reduce unnecessary legal fees, and ultimately secure the trademark protection you need to build a lasting business.

item.title: Anthropic CEO says AI centralizes by nature and open models just shift power to whoever owns the chips [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: An open fight over AI regulation has broken out on X. Investor Gavin Baker, former White House adviser David Sacks, and Meta researcher Yann LeCun accuse Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei of using fear rhetoric to buy himself a regulatory advantage. Amodei counters that regulation can also rein in corporate power, and that open models alone just shift power toward the players with the most computing muscle. The article Anthropic CEO says AI centralizes by nature and open models just shift power to whoever owns the chips appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: DOJ probes Andreessen Horowitz over partners sitting on competing AI boards
item.description: Andreessen Horowitz is the focus of an antitrust probe by the US Justice Department. The charge is that the firm's partners sit on the boards of competing data firms Databricks and Fivetran at the same time. The venture capital firm's close ties to the Trump administration add a twist, since it has actively lobbied for the administration's AI deregulation. The article DOJ probes Andreessen Horowitz over partners sitting on competing AI boards appeared first on The Decoder.
